title: Local asymmetry in interference as a probe of quantum probability
summary: Quantum interference provides one of the most sensitive probes of quantum mechanics. While linear superposition fixes the positions and quadratic curvature of interference fringes, it remains unclear whether the probabilistic postulate itself, the Born rule, can be tested through finer, local features of interference patterns. Here we show that a minimal deformation of quantum probability gives rise to a robust and symmetry-protected signature: a left-right asymmetry in the local shape of interference fringes. Remarkably, this effect leaves the linear Schrödinger dynamics intact and does not shift fringe positions or modify their quadratic curvature. Instead, it appears exclusively as a cubic skewness of local intensity profiles, providing a clean and falsifiable observable. We demonstrate this behavior within a controlled realization that preserves linear dynamics while minimally deforming the probabilistic assignment. The resulting signature is universal, scale insensitive, and cannot be mimicked by conventional sources of experimental noise. Our results identify local asymmetry in interference as a direct probe of quantum probability itself, suggesting that features often regarded as removable imperfections may encode fundamental information beyond fringe positions and widths.

AI.tldr: Local asymmetry in interference fringes provides a direct test of the Born rule, with cubic skewness serving as a clean signature that preserves Schrödinger dynamics while minimally deforming quantum probability.
AI.motivation: To test the fundamental probabilistic postulate of quantum mechanics (the Born rule) beyond traditional interference measurements that only probe linear superposition and quadratic curvature of fringes.
AI.method: Introduce a minimal deformation of quantum probability that preserves linear Schrödinger dynamics while modifying the probabilistic assignment, leading to cubic skewness in local interference fringe profiles without affecting fringe positions or quadratic curvature.
AI.result: The deformation produces a robust left-right asymmetry in interference fringes appearing exclusively as cubic skewness, which is universal, scale-insensitive, and distinguishable from conventional experimental noise.
AI.conclusion: Local asymmetry in interference patterns provides a direct probe of quantum probability itself, suggesting that features typically considered imperfections may encode fundamental information about the Born rule.

title: Assessing Spatiotemporally Correlated Noise in Superconducting Qubits via Pulse-Based Quantum Noise Spectroscopy
summary: Spatiotemporally correlated errors are widespread in quantum devices and are particularly adversarial to error correcting schemes. To characterize these errors, we propose and validate a nonparametric quantum noise spectroscopy (QNS) protocol to estimate both spectra and static errors associated with spatiotemporally correlated dephasing noise and fluctuating quantum crosstalk on two qubits. Our scheme reconstructs the real and imaginary components of the two-qubit cross-spectrum by using fixed total time pulse sequences and single qubit and joint two-qubit measurements to separately resolve spatially correlated noise processes. We benchmark our protocol by reconstructing the spectra of spatiotemporally correlated noise processes engineered via the Schrödinger Wave Autoregressive Moving Average technique, emulating dephasing errors. Furthermore, we show that the protocol can outperform existing comb-based QNS protocols. Our results demonstrate the utility of our protocol in characterizing spatiotemporally correlated noise and quantum crosstalk in a multi-qubit device for potential use in noise-adapted control or error protection schemes.

AI.tldr: Nonparametric quantum noise spectroscopy protocol for characterizing spatiotemporally correlated dephasing noise and quantum crosstalk in multi-qubit devices using fixed-time pulse sequences and joint measurements.
AI.motivation: Spatiotemporally correlated errors are widespread in quantum devices and particularly adversarial to error correcting schemes, requiring better characterization methods.
AI.method: Proposes a nonparametric quantum noise spectroscopy protocol that reconstructs real and imaginary components of two-qubit cross-spectrum using fixed total time pulse sequences, single qubit measurements, and joint two-qubit measurements to separately resolve spatially correlated noise processes.
AI.result: Protocol validated by reconstructing spectra of engineered spatiotemporally correlated noise processes using Schrödinger Wave Autoregressive Moving Average technique, and shown to outperform existing comb-based QNS protocols.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates utility of the protocol for characterizing spatiotemporally correlated noise and quantum crosstalk in multi-qubit devices for potential use in noise-adapted control or error protection schemes.

title: Semidefinite block-matrix relaxations for computing quantum correlations
summary: Bounding the correlations predicted by quantum theory is an important challenge in quantum information science. Today's leading approach is semidefinite programming relaxations, but existing methods still cannot account for many relevant types of constraints. Here, we propose a semidefinite relaxation methodology that can incorporate a breadth of constraints needed in various quantum correlation problems, thereby generalising the seminal Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy. It yields useful results at reasonable computational cost. We showcase the methodology and its features by using it to address five different quantum information problems. These are (i) entanglement witnessing from imperfect measurement devices, (ii) certifying measurements from fidelity-constrained sources, (iii) computing dimensionality in genuine multi-particle entangled states, (iv) benchmarking dimensionality for state preparation devices, and (v) finding uncertainty relations for nearly anti-commuting observables. These applications reflect both the usefulness and versatility of the methodology, as well as its potential for broader relevance in the field.

AI.tldr: A new semidefinite programming relaxation methodology that generalizes the NPA hierarchy to incorporate diverse constraints for bounding quantum correlations, demonstrated across five quantum information applications.
AI.motivation: Existing semidefinite programming relaxations for bounding quantum correlations cannot account for many relevant constraint types needed in practical quantum information problems, limiting their applicability.
AI.method: Proposes a generalized semidefinite relaxation methodology that extends the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to incorporate a broader range of constraints, enabling computational analysis of quantum correlations under various practical limitations.
AI.result: The methodology yields useful results at reasonable computational cost and is successfully applied to five distinct quantum information problems: entanglement witnessing with imperfect devices, measurement certification from fidelity-constrained sources, computing dimensionality in genuine multi-particle entangled states, benchmarking dimensionality for state preparation devices, and finding uncertainty relations for nearly anti-commuting observables.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methodology demonstrates both usefulness and versatility across diverse quantum information applications, offering potential for broader relevance in the field by overcoming limitations of existing constraint-handling approaches in quantum correlation analysis.

title: Approximate virtual quantum broadcasting
comment: 9+6 pages. PDF-only upload due to arXiv technical issues; source will be uploaded in subsequent revision
summary: The no-broadcasting theorem, a fundamental limitation on the communication of quantum information, holds that a physical process cannot broadcast copies of an unknown quantum state to two or more receivers. Recent work has explored ways of circumventing this limitation using "virtual" implementations of non-physical processes using measurement and data-processing on statistical samples of the unknown input. However, the statistical fluctuations of this data degrades the virtual copies so much that the protocol effectively depletes, rather than proliferate, the sample size -- thereby rendering it worse than the "naive" approach of splitting the given sample and sending a subsample to each receiver. In this work, we circumvent this flaw by allowing a small amount of systematic bias in the broadcast data, resulting in approximate virtual copies. We provide efficient semidefinite programs (SDP's) to determine the minimum sample size required to keep the approximation error below a desired threshold and vice versa. For reasonably small error values, we find approximate virtual broadcasting to be viable with sample sizes smaller than naive sample-splitting would demand. Along the way, we prove several symmetry-based simplifications to the problem, allowing optimal approximate broadcasting to be characterized in terms of the simple class of depolarizing channels.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces approximate virtual broadcasting as a method to circumvent the no-broadcasting theorem by allowing systematic bias, showing it requires smaller sample sizes than naive splitting for reasonable error thresholds.
AI.motivation: The no-broadcasting theorem prevents broadcasting unknown quantum states. Previous virtual implementations using measurement and data-processing suffer from statistical fluctuations that degrade copies and deplete sample size, making them worse than naive sample-splitting.
AI.method: Introduces approximate virtual broadcasting by allowing systematic bias in broadcast data, uses efficient semidefinite programs (SDPs) to determine minimum sample size for desired error thresholds, proves symmetry-based simplifications reducing the problem to depolarizing channels.
AI.result: For reasonably small error values, approximate virtual broadcasting is viable with sample sizes smaller than naive sample-splitting demands. Optimal approximate broadcasting can be characterized using depolarizing channels.
AI.conclusion: Approximate virtual broadcasting with controlled systematic bias provides a practical way to circumvent the no-broadcasting theorem, offering advantages over naive approaches when error tolerances are reasonable.

title: A Federated Many-to-One Hopfield model for associative Neural Networks
summary: Federated learning enables collaborative training without sharing raw data, but struggles under client heterogeneity and streaming distribution shifts, where drift and novel data can impair convergence and cause forgetting. We propose a federated associative-memory framework that learns shared archetypes in heterogeneous, continual settings, where client data are independent but not necessarily balanced. Each client encodes its experience as a low-rank Hebbian operator, sent to a central server for aggregation and factorization into global archetypes. This approach preserves privacy, avoids centralized replay buffers, and is robust to small, noisy, or evolving datasets. We cast aggregation as a low-rank-plus-noise spectral inference problem, deriving theoretical thresholds for detectability and retrieval robustness. An entropy-based controller balances stability and plasticity in streaming regimes. Experiments with heterogeneous clients, drift, and novelty show improved global archetype reconstruction and associative retrieval, supporting the spectral view of federated consolidation.

AI.tldr: Federated associative-memory framework learns shared archetypes in heterogeneous, continual settings using low-rank Hebbian operators and spectral inference, with entropy-based control for stability-plasticity balance.
AI.motivation: Federated learning struggles with client heterogeneity and streaming distribution shifts, where drift and novel data impair convergence and cause forgetting. Need for privacy-preserving approach that handles evolving data without centralized replay buffers.
AI.method: Clients encode experience as low-rank Hebbian operators, sent to server for aggregation and factorization into global archetypes. Cast aggregation as low-rank-plus-noise spectral inference problem with theoretical detectability thresholds. Use entropy-based controller for stability-plasticity balance in streaming regimes.
AI.result: Improved global archetype reconstruction and associative retrieval in experiments with heterogeneous clients, drift, and novelty. Supports spectral view of federated consolidation.
AI.conclusion: Proposed federated associative-memory framework effectively handles heterogeneity and continual learning in federated settings, providing privacy preservation, robustness to small/noisy/evolving datasets, and theoretical guarantees for archetype detection and retrieval.

title: Heralded quasi-deterministic entanglement sources based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion
summary: A double-heralding technique is presented for producing heralded entangled photon pairs from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC). Compared to the swap-heralded schemes studied in previous cascaded SPDC and zero-added-loss multiplexing (ZALM) proposals, this double-heralding technique is found to yield the most resource-efficient implementation in terms of minimizing the total number of sources and detectors required to achieve a specified rate and fidelity. This is achieved by reducing the number of modes and mode-sorting optics needed on the heralding path. Specifically, by immediately detecting any two signal photons from an array of down-converters, the corresponding idler photons can be projected onto an anti-correlated pair state which is shown to be unitarily equivalent to the state produced by swap-heralded sources, and hence can be used directly for long-range entanglement distribution in a ZALM architecture. Quasi-deterministic operation through two distinct multiplexing techniques is analyzed. The analysis derives expressions for the heralded pair probability and fidelity assuming realistic detectors with losses, dark counts, and partial photon number resolution (PNR), providing a framework for implementation of the source on a photonic integrated circuit (PIC).

AI.tldr: Double-heralding technique for producing heralded entangled photon pairs from SPDC that is more resource-efficient than previous schemes by reducing modes and mode-sorting optics on heralding path.
AI.motivation: To develop a more resource-efficient method for producing heralded entangled photon pairs from SPDC compared to previous cascaded SPDC and ZALM proposals, minimizing the total number of sources and detectors required for specified rate and fidelity.
AI.method: Double-heralding technique where any two signal photons from an array of down-converters are immediately detected, projecting corresponding idler photons onto anti-correlated pair states that are unitarily equivalent to swap-heralded source states. Analyzes quasi-deterministic operation through two distinct multiplexing techniques.
AI.result: The technique yields the most resource-efficient implementation in terms of minimizing total number of sources and detectors required to achieve specified rate and fidelity. Derives expressions for heralded pair probability and fidelity assuming realistic detectors with losses, dark counts, and partial PNR.
AI.conclusion: Double-heralding technique provides framework for implementation on photonic integrated circuits, enabling direct use for long-range entanglement distribution in ZALM architecture with improved resource efficiency.

title: Continuous Specialization Transition in the Soft Committee Machine with ReLU Activation
summary: We analyze the soft committee machine with Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation by means of the replica method. In a realizable teacher--student setting, we compute the quenched free energy within a replica-symmetric ansatz and obtain the typical generalization behavior from the saddle-point equations for the macroscopic order parameters. The system exhibits a transition from an unspecialized symmetric phase to a specialized phase in which the permutation symmetry among hidden units is broken. We determine the critical training-set size as a function of the inverse training temperature and derive analytic expressions both near the transition and in the asymptotic large-sample regime. Unlike the corresponding model with sigmoidal activations, which undergoes a first-order transition, the ReLU soft committee machine shows a continuous specialization transition. These results show that the activation function plays a decisive role in the phase structure and generalization behavior of multilayer networks.

AI.tldr: Replica analysis of ReLU soft committee machine reveals continuous specialization transition from symmetric to specialized phase, contrasting with first-order transition in sigmoidal networks.
AI.motivation: To understand how activation functions affect the phase structure and generalization behavior of multilayer neural networks, specifically comparing ReLU with sigmoidal activations in a teacher-student framework.
AI.method: Replica method applied to soft committee machine with ReLU activation in realizable teacher-student setting; replica-symmetric ansatz used to compute quenched free energy; saddle-point equations derived for macroscopic order parameters.
AI.result: System exhibits transition from unspecialized symmetric phase to specialized phase with broken permutation symmetry; critical training-set size determined as function of inverse training temperature; analytic expressions derived near transition and in large-sample regime; ReLU shows continuous specialization transition unlike first-order transition in sigmoidal networks.
AI.conclusion: Activation function plays decisive role in phase structure and generalization behavior of multilayer networks, with ReLU exhibiting qualitatively different (continuous) specialization transition compared to sigmoidal activations.

title: Preserving MWPM-Decodability in Fault-Equivalent Rewrites
summary:
Decoding a quantum error correction code is generally NP-hard, but corrections must be applied at a high frequency to suppress noise successfully. Matchable codes, like the surface code, exhibit a special structure that makes it possible to efficiently, approximately solve the decoding problem through minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM). However, this efficiency-enabling property can be lost when constructing implementations for fault-tolerant gadgets such as syndrome-extraction circuits or logical operations.
  In this work, we take a circuit-centric perspective to formalise how the decoding problem changes when applying ZX rewrites to a ZX diagram with a given detector basis. We demonstrate a set of rewrites that preserve MWPM-decodability of circuits and show that these matchability-preserving rewrites can be used to fault-tolerantly extract quantum circuits from phase-free ZX diagrams. In particular, this allows us to build efficiently decodable, fault-tolerant syndrome-extraction circuits for matchable codes.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a circuit-centric approach to preserve MWPM-decodability in fault-tolerant quantum circuits by using ZX rewrites that maintain matchability properties.
AI.motivation: While matchable codes like surface codes enable efficient decoding via MWPM, this property can be lost when implementing fault-tolerant gadgets such as syndrome-extraction circuits or logical operations, creating a need for methods that preserve decodability during circuit construction.
AI.method: The authors adopt a circuit-centric perspective to formalize how decoding problems change with ZX rewrites applied to ZX diagrams with given detector bases. They identify and demonstrate a set of rewrites that preserve MWPM-decodability and use these matchability-preserving rewrites to fault-tolerantly extract quantum circuits from phase-free ZX diagrams.
AI.result: The method enables construction of efficiently decodable, fault-tolerant syndrome-extraction circuits for matchable codes by preserving the structural properties that make MWPM decoding possible.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a systematic way to maintain efficient decodability when implementing fault-tolerant quantum circuits, addressing a key challenge in practical quantum error correction implementations for matchable codes.

title: Stabilizer Formalism for EAQECCs with Noise ebits
summary: We introduce a stabilizer formalism for EAQECCs with noise ebits, using special subgroups of product groups of two Pauli groups. This formalism includes the two coding schemes,given by Lai and Brun (C.Y. Lai and T. A. Brun, PHYSICAL REVIEW A 86, 032319 (2012)), for EAQECCs with imperfect ebits as special cases. Then two equivalent formalisms of the formalism are derived in nomenclature of sympletic geometry and additive codes. We apply this theory to construct some EAQECCs with noise ebits, and analyze their performance.

AI.tldr: A stabilizer formalism for entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs) with noisy ebits, generalizing previous schemes and providing equivalent symplectic geometry and additive code formulations.
AI.motivation: To develop a comprehensive mathematical framework for EAQECCs that accounts for imperfect entanglement resources (noisy ebits), generalizing existing schemes by Lai and Brun and enabling systematic code construction and performance analysis.
AI.method: Introduces a stabilizer formalism using special subgroups of product groups of two Pauli groups, derives two equivalent formalisms in symplectic geometry and additive code nomenclature, then applies the theory to construct specific EAQECCs with noise ebits.
AI.result: The formalism encompasses Lai and Brun's two coding schemes as special cases, provides equivalent mathematical representations, and enables construction of practical EAQECCs with noisy ebits along with performance analysis.
AI.conclusion: A unified stabilizer framework for EAQECCs with imperfect entanglement has been established, offering multiple equivalent mathematical perspectives and practical applications for quantum error correction with noisy resources.

title: Universal method for optimized robustness in self-testing of quantum resources
summary: Self-testing is a phenomenon where the use of specific quantum states or measurements can be inferred solely from the correlations they generate. We introduce a universal method for conducting robustness analysis in the self-testing of various quantum resources. Unlike previous numerical approaches, which rely on selecting specific isometries, our method optimizes over equivalence transformations, thereby leading to tighter robustness bounds. This optimization employs the well-established technique of semidefinite programming relaxations for non-commuting polynomial optimization. Our method can be universally applied to diverse self-testing settings, including steerable assemblages in the Bell scenario, constellations of quantum states in the prepare-and-measure scenario, and entangled states in the steering scenario. We demonstrate the method's capability to surpass previously reported robustness bounds across a range of concrete examples.

AI.tldr: A universal method for robustness analysis in quantum self-testing using semidefinite programming relaxations that optimizes over equivalence transformations to achieve tighter bounds across various scenarios.
AI.motivation: Existing numerical approaches for robustness analysis in quantum self-testing rely on selecting specific isometries, which may not yield optimal robustness bounds. There's a need for a more universal method that can provide tighter bounds across diverse self-testing scenarios.
AI.method: The method uses semidefinite programming relaxations for non-commuting polynomial optimization to optimize over equivalence transformations rather than specific isometries. This universal approach can be applied to various self-testing settings including steerable assemblages in Bell scenarios, quantum state constellations in prepare-and-measure scenarios, and entangled states in steering scenarios.
AI.result: The method demonstrates capability to surpass previously reported robustness bounds across a range of concrete examples, showing improved performance over previous numerical approaches that rely on specific isometry selection.
AI.conclusion: The introduced universal method provides tighter robustness bounds for quantum self-testing by optimizing over equivalence transformations using semidefinite programming relaxations, offering improved analysis capabilities across diverse quantum resource self-testing scenarios.

title: Beyond-Ten-Hour Coherence in a Decoherence-Free Trapped-Ion Clock Qubit
summary: Quantum systems promise to revolutionize information processing science and technology [1-3]. The preservation of quantum coherence, the defining property of qubits, fundamentally constrains the performance of quantum information processing with quantum memories [4]. While trapped atomic ions theoretically support million-year coherence based on spontaneous emission [5-7], experimental demonstrations have reached far less, only about an hour [8-13]. Here we combine clock-state qubits with decoherence-free subspace (DFS) encoding to achieve coherence exceeding ten hours. Using correlation-based phase tracking in 171Yb+ ion pairs sympathetically cooled by 138Ba+ ion, we demonstrate this without magnetic shielding or enhanced microwave phase stabilization that previously limited coherence times. DFS encoding references the qubit phase to the inter-ion energy difference to reject microwave phase noise and common-mode magnetic fluctuations, while clock states provide environmental insensitivity. Throughout measurements extended to 1600 seconds, we observe minimal coherence decay, with exponential fits yielding a coherence time of (3.77 +/- 1.09) x 10^4 seconds. Our results establish DFS encoding as a form of passive error correction that eliminates technical noise constraints, unlocking the million-year coherence potential of atomic ions for scalable quantum information processing.

AI.tldr: DFS encoding with clock-state qubits achieves >10-hour coherence in trapped ions without magnetic shielding, unlocking million-year coherence potential.
AI.motivation: Quantum coherence preservation is fundamental to quantum information processing. While trapped atomic ions theoretically support million-year coherence, experimental demonstrations have been limited to about an hour due to technical noise constraints.
AI.method: Combined clock-state qubits with decoherence-free subspace (DFS) encoding using 171Yb+ ion pairs sympathetically cooled by 138Ba+ ion. Used correlation-based phase tracking to reference qubit phase to inter-ion energy difference, rejecting microwave phase noise and common-mode magnetic fluctuations without magnetic shielding or enhanced microwave phase stabilization.
AI.result: Achieved coherence exceeding ten hours with minimal decay observed up to 1600 seconds. Exponential fits yielded coherence time of (3.77 ± 1.09) × 10^4 seconds (~10.5 hours), far exceeding previous experimental demonstrations.
AI.conclusion: DFS encoding serves as passive error correction that eliminates technical noise constraints, unlocking the million-year coherence potential of atomic ions for scalable quantum information processing.

title: Transfer of nonlocality and entanglement of an open three-qubit W state in the background of dilaton black hole
summary: Constrained by the complexity of theoretical calculations, current research on genuine tripartite nonlocality (GTN) within the relativistic framework concentrates mainly on Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-like states, with few studies addressing W states or even general tripartite states. In this paper, we apply numerical methods to investigate how environmental decoherence and spacetime dilaton influence GTN and genuine tripartite entanglement (GTE) of W states. Our results show that GTN in the physically accessible region displays a ``sudden death phenomenon'' and that sufficiently strong decoherence completely destroys GTN. By contrast, GTE in the physically accessible region initially remains unchanged and then decays only when the dilaton parameter becomes large. Notably, the GTN and GTE in the physically accessible region can be enhanced by adjusting the decoherence parameter. Furthermore, we also find that the GTN in the physically inaccessible region cannot be generated, whereas the GTE will be produced there. This implies that GTE can cross the event horizon of a black hole and realize the redistribution of quantum entanglement. Finally, we further discuss whether the GTN can be transferred to the bipartite subsystem of the system.

AI.tldr: Numerical study shows W states' genuine tripartite nonlocality (GTN) experiences sudden death under decoherence and spacetime dilation, while genuine tripartite entanglement (GTE) persists longer and can cross black hole event horizons.
AI.motivation: Current relativistic GTN research focuses mainly on GHZ-like states, with limited investigation of W states or general tripartite states due to theoretical complexity. This study aims to address this gap by examining how environmental decoherence and spacetime dilation affect GTN and GTE in W states.
AI.method: Applied numerical methods to investigate the effects of environmental decoherence and spacetime dilaton on GTN and GTE of W states. Analyzed both physically accessible and inaccessible regions relative to black hole event horizons.
AI.result: GTN in accessible regions shows sudden death phenomenon and can be completely destroyed by strong decoherence. GTE initially remains unchanged then decays with large dilation parameters. Both GTN and GTE can be enhanced by adjusting decoherence parameters. GTN cannot be generated in inaccessible regions, but GTE can be produced there, enabling entanglement redistribution across event horizons.
AI.conclusion: GTE exhibits greater robustness than GTN under relativistic effects and can cross black hole event horizons, enabling quantum entanglement redistribution. GTN shows more fragility with sudden death behavior and cannot be transferred to inaccessible regions. The study provides insights into quantum information behavior in curved spacetime.

title: Structure and Classification of Matrix Product Quantum Channels
summary: We develop a framework for Matrix Product Quantum Channels (MPQCs), a one-dimensional tensor-network description of completely positive, trace-preserving maps. We focus on translation-invariant channels, generated by a single repeated tensor, that admit a local purification. We show that their purifying isometry can always be implemented by a constant-depth brickwork quantum circuit, implying that such channels generate only short-range correlations. In contrast to the unitary setting, where one-dimensional quantum cellular automata (in one-to-one correspondence with matrix product unitaries) carry a nontrivial index, we prove that all locally purified channels belong to a single phase, that is, they can be continuously deformed into one another. We then extend the framework to a broader class of translation-invariant channels capable of generating long-range entanglement and show that these remain deterministically implementable in constant depth using two rounds of measurements and feedforward.

AI.tldr: MPQCs are tensor-network descriptions of quantum channels; translation-invariant locally purified channels generate only short-range correlations and belong to a single phase, unlike unitary QCA which have nontrivial index.
AI.motivation: To develop a tensor-network framework for describing quantum channels, particularly translation-invariant ones, and understand their correlation properties and classification compared to unitary quantum cellular automata.
AI.method: Develop Matrix Product Quantum Channels (MPQCs) framework using tensor networks, focus on translation-invariant channels with local purification, analyze their purifying isometry implementation via constant-depth brickwork circuits, and extend to channels generating long-range entanglement.
AI.result: Locally purified MPQCs generate only short-range correlations and belong to a single phase (can be continuously deformed into each other), unlike unitary QCA with nontrivial index. Extended channels with long-range entanglement remain implementable in constant depth using measurements and feedforward.
AI.conclusion: MPQCs provide a powerful framework for studying quantum channels; locally purified channels form a single phase with limited correlation generation, while extended channels can create long-range entanglement while maintaining constant-depth implementability.

title: Linear-optical generation of hybrid GKP entanglement from small-amplitude cat states
summary: Hybrid bosonic codes combining bosonic codes with photon states offer a promising pathway for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, the efficient generation of such states in optical setups remains technically challenging due to the requirement for complex non-Gaussian resources. In this paper, we propose a novel scheme to efficiently generate hybrid entangled states between a GKP qubit and a photon-number state using small-amplitude cat states as the primary resource. We apply a breeding process using small-amplitude cat states to increase the non-Gaussianity of the input states. This method requires only linear optical elements and homodyne measurements. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this protocol can be extended to generate hybrid qudit states. This scheme has the potential to provide a resource-efficient and experimentally attractive route toward implementing hybrid quantum error correction.

AI.tldr: Efficient generation of hybrid bosonic codes using small-amplitude cat states, linear optics, and homodyne measurements for quantum error correction.
AI.motivation: Hybrid bosonic codes combining bosonic codes with photon states are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but efficient generation remains challenging due to complex non-Gaussian resource requirements.
AI.method: Proposes a scheme using small-amplitude cat states as primary resource, applying a breeding process to increase non-Gaussianity, requiring only linear optical elements and homodyne measurements.
AI.result: Efficient generation of hybrid entangled states between GKP qubits and photon-number states, with extension to hybrid qudit states.
AI.conclusion: The scheme provides a resource-efficient and experimentally attractive route toward implementing hybrid quantum error correction.

title: SDP bounds on quantum codes: rational certificates
summary: A fundamental problem in quantum coding theory is to determine the maximum size of quantum codes of given block length and distance. A recent work introduced bounds based on semidefinite programming, strengthening the well-known quantum linear programming bounds. However, floating-point inaccuracies prevent the extraction of rigorous non-existence proofs from the numerical methods. Here, we address this by providing rational infeasibility certificates for a range of quantum codes. Using a clustered low-rank solver with heuristic rounding to algebraic expressions, we can improve upon $18$ upper bounds on the maximum size of $n$-qubit codes with $6 \leq n \leq 19$. Our work highlights the practicality and scalability of semidefinite programming for quantum coding bounds.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to compute rigorous upper bounds on quantum code sizes using rational infeasibility certificates from semidefinite programming, improving 18 bounds for n-qubit codes (6 ≤ n ≤ 19).
AI.motivation: To address the problem of floating-point inaccuracies preventing rigorous non-existence proofs from numerical semidefinite programming methods in quantum coding theory, which previously limited the extraction of exact bounds.
AI.method: Uses rational infeasibility certificates derived from semidefinite programming with a clustered low-rank solver and heuristic rounding to algebraic expressions to obtain rigorous bounds.
AI.result: Improved 18 upper bounds on the maximum size of n-qubit codes for 6 ≤ n ≤ 19, demonstrating the practicality and scalability of the approach.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes that semidefinite programming with rational infeasibility certificates provides a practical and scalable method for obtaining rigorous quantum coding bounds, overcoming previous limitations from floating-point inaccuracies.

title: Quantum gyroscope based on three-dimensional rotation induced Berry phase
summary: Solid-spin defects in diamond provide long coherence times and room-temperature optical initialization and readout, making them an attractive platform for compact solid-state quantum gyroscopes. A central challenge for NV-based gyroscopes is that the rotation-induced signal is weak, while near-resonant operation, although enhancing the response, can induce nonadiabatic transitions that degrade the accumulated geometric phase and readout fidelity. Here we investigate a levitated diamond under three-dimensional rotation, in which intrinsic ${}^{14}\mathrm{N}$ nuclear spins associated with NV centers act as sensing qubits. We show that the rotation is encoded in a geometric (Berry) phase and identify a near-resonant regime with strongly enhanced phase response. To suppress the resulting nonadiabatic leakage, we introduce a counter-diabatic protocol derived from the Kato gauge potential. This enables robust geometric-phase accumulation and improves the sensitivity by four orders of magnitude relative to the conventional detuned protocol. We further evaluate the achievable sensitivity and the dominant experimental limitations, including decoherence and protocol overhead, thereby establishing a realistic route toward high-performance NV-based solid-state quantum gyroscopes.

AI.tldr: NV-center-based quantum gyroscope using geometric phase with counter-diabatic protocol achieves 4 orders of magnitude sensitivity improvement.
AI.motivation: NV centers in diamond offer long coherence times and room-temperature optical readout for compact quantum gyroscopes, but rotation signals are weak and near-resonant operation causes nonadiabatic transitions that degrade performance.
AI.method: Use levitated diamond with 3D rotation, employing intrinsic 14N nuclear spins as sensing qubits. Rotation is encoded in geometric (Berry) phase. Introduce counter-diabatic protocol derived from Kato gauge potential to suppress nonadiabatic leakage in near-resonant regime.
AI.result: Counter-diabatic protocol enables robust geometric-phase accumulation and improves sensitivity by four orders of magnitude relative to conventional detuned protocol. Achievable sensitivity and experimental limitations (decoherence, protocol overhead) are evaluated.
AI.conclusion: The approach establishes a realistic route toward high-performance NV-based solid-state quantum gyroscopes by addressing key challenges of weak rotation signals and nonadiabatic transitions.

title: Efficiently Computable Strategies and Limits for Bosonic Channel Discrimination
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures and 20 pages of appendices
summary: Discriminating between noisy quantum processes is a central primitive for quantum communication, metrology, and computing. While discrimination limits for finite-dimensional channels are well understood, the continuous-variable setting, particularly under experimentally relevant energy constraints, remains significantly less developed. In this work, we establish an energy-constrained chain rule for the Belavkin-Staszewski channel divergence, which yields a fundamental upper bound on the error exponents achievable by fully adaptive, energy-constrained quantum channel discrimination protocols. We then derive efficiently computable bounds on asymmetric error exponents for energy-constrained discrimination of bosonic dephasing and loss-dephasing channels. Specifically, we show that three operationally relevant quantities -- the measured relative entropy, the Umegaki relative entropy, and the geometric Renyi divergence -- admit semidefinite program (SDP) formulations when the input energy is bounded and the Hilbert space is suitably truncated. Applying these tools, we demonstrate that optimal probes for these channels under energy constraints are Fock-diagonal, and we also enable numerically precise evaluation of bounds on achievable error exponents across discrimination strategies ranging from separable to fully adaptive. The resulting SDPs provide practical benchmarks for quantum-limited sensing in low-energy bosonic platforms.

AI.tldr: Establishes energy-constrained discrimination bounds for bosonic quantum channels via SDP formulations of channel divergences, enabling practical benchmarks for quantum sensing.
AI.motivation: Quantum channel discrimination is fundamental for quantum technologies, but continuous-variable settings under energy constraints lack developed discrimination limits compared to finite-dimensional cases.
AI.method: Derives energy-constrained chain rule for Belavkin-Staszewski divergence; formulates measured relative entropy, Umegaki relative entropy, and geometric Renyi divergence as semidefinite programs under energy constraints with Hilbert space truncation.
AI.result: Shows optimal probes for bosonic dephasing and loss-dephasing channels under energy constraints are Fock-diagonal; provides numerically precise bounds on error exponents across discrimination strategies from separable to fully adaptive.
AI.conclusion: Developed SDP-based framework provides practical benchmarks for quantum-limited sensing in low-energy bosonic platforms, advancing continuous-variable channel discrimination theory.

title: One-parameter counterexamples to the refined Bessis-Moussa-Villani conjecture
summary: The Bessis-Moussa-Villani (BMV) conjecture, originating in quantum statistical mechanics, was proved by Stahl after an influential reformulation by Lieb and Seiringer. A later refinement asks whether the normalized average over all words with $n$ letters $A$ and $m$ letters $B$ is always bounded above by $\mathrm{tr}(A^nB^m)$ and below by $\mathrm{tr}\exp(n\log A+m\log B)$. We study a specific one-parameter family $(A_x, B_x)$ and derive exact closed formulas for both sides of the first inequality when $(n,m)=(5,5)$. In particular, $x=10^{-3}$ gives a counterexample.

AI.tldr: The paper studies a specific counterexample to a refined BMV conjecture inequality, showing that the normalized average over words with 5 A's and 5 B's is not always bounded above by tr(A⁵B⁵) for a particular parameter value.
AI.motivation: To investigate a refined version of the Bessis-Moussa-Villani (BMV) conjecture, which asks whether the normalized average over all words with n letters A and m letters B is bounded above by tr(AⁿBᵐ) and below by tr(exp(n log A + m log B)).
AI.method: Study a specific one-parameter family (A_x, B_x) and derive exact closed formulas for both sides of the first inequality when (n,m) = (5,5).
AI.result: Found that x = 10⁻³ gives a counterexample to the inequality, demonstrating that the normalized average is not always bounded above by tr(A⁵B⁵).
AI.conclusion: The refined BMV conjecture inequality fails for the specific case (n,m) = (5,5) with the parameter value x = 10⁻³, providing a counterexample to the proposed bound.

title: Adaptive Parallelism-Aware Qubit Routing for Ion Trap QCCD Architectures
summary: Trapped-ion Quantum Charge-Coupled Device (QCCD) architectures promise scalability through interconnected trap zones and dynamic ion transport; however, this transport capability creates a complex compilation challenge: how to move qubits efficiently without degrading fidelity. We introduce a routing strategy that turns this challenge into an advantage by exploiting operational parallelism across traps while adapting to both algorithmic structure and device topology through a configurable multi-parameter scoring mechanism. Across a broad suite of benchmarks and QCCD layouts, the method consistently reduces ion-transport overhead and improves execution fidelity, outperforming state-of-the-art routing techniques. These results highlight that explicitly balancing movement overhead and execution parallelism under architectural constraints is key to unlocking the full potential of modular trapped-ion quantum processors.

AI.tldr: A routing strategy for trapped-ion QCCD architectures that exploits operational parallelism across traps to reduce transport overhead and improve execution fidelity, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques.
AI.motivation: Trapped-ion QCCD architectures enable scalability through interconnected trap zones and dynamic ion transport, but this transport capability creates complex compilation challenges for moving qubits efficiently without degrading fidelity.
AI.method: Introduces a routing strategy that exploits operational parallelism across traps while adapting to both algorithmic structure and device topology through a configurable multi-parameter scoring mechanism.
AI.result: Across broad benchmarks and QCCD layouts, the method consistently reduces ion-transport overhead and improves execution fidelity, outperforming state-of-the-art routing techniques.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly balancing movement overhead and execution parallelism under architectural constraints is key to unlocking the full potential of modular trapped-ion quantum processors.

title: Stone-in-Waiting: A Cloud-Based Accelerator for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
summary: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and its advanced variant, the Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (QAOA), are major research topics in the current era of Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) computing. However, the problem of initializing their parameters remains unresolved. Motivated by the combinatorial optimization task in the 6th MindSpore Quantum Computing Hackathon (2024), this paper proposes Stone-in-Waiting, a cloud-based accelerator for obtaining high-quality initial parameters for QAOA. Internally, the accelerator builds on state-of-the-art theories and methods for parameter determination and integrates four self-developed algorithms for QAOA parameter initialization, mainly based on Bayesian methods, nearest-neighbor methods, and metric learning. Compared with the Baseline Algorithm, the generated parameters improve the score by 40.19%. Externally, the accelerator offers both a web interface and an API, providing flexible and convenient access for users to test and develop related experiments and applications. This paper presents the design principles and methods of Stone-in-Waiting, demonstrates its functional characteristics, compares the strengths and weaknesses of the four proposed algorithms, and validates the overall system performance through experiments.

AI.tldr: Stone-in-Waiting is a cloud-based accelerator that provides high-quality initial parameters for QAOA using four self-developed algorithms based on Bayesian methods, nearest-neighbor techniques, and metric learning, achieving 40.19% improvement over baseline.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the unresolved problem of parameter initialization for QAOA and its variant QAOA in NISQ computing, motivated by combinatorial optimization tasks from the 6th MindSpore Quantum Computing Hackathon (2024).
AI.method: Proposes Stone-in-Waiting, a cloud-based accelerator that integrates four self-developed algorithms for QAOA parameter initialization based on Bayesian methods, nearest-neighbor methods, and metric learning, with both web interface and API access.
AI.result: The generated parameters improve the score by 40.19% compared to the Baseline Algorithm, with comprehensive comparison of the four proposed algorithms' strengths and weaknesses, and validation of overall system performance.
AI.conclusion: Stone-in-Waiting provides an effective cloud-based solution for QAOA parameter initialization, offering significant performance improvements and flexible access through web interface and API for quantum computing applications.

title: Cryptanalysis of four arbitrated quantum signature schemes
summary:
Arbitrated quantum signature (AQS) schemes aim at ensuring the authenticity of a message with the help of an arbitrator. Moreover, they aim at preventing repudiation, both from a sender that denies the origin of a message, and from a receiver who disavows its reception. Such protocols use quantum communication and are often designed to protect quantum messages. In this paper, we study four recently submitted AQS schemes and propose attacks on their security.
  Firstly, we look at Zhang, Sun, Zhang and Jia's AQS scheme which aims at signing quantum messages with chained CNOT encryption. We show that the sender can repudiate her messages and make false allegation of reception. Moreover, we show that a dishonest receiver can forge signatures.
  Secondly, we analyse Ding, Xin, Yang and Sang's AQS protocol to sign classical messages based on GHZ states. We show that both the sender and the receiver have simple repudiation strategies.
  Thirdly, we study Lu, Li, Yu and Han's AQS scheme that uses controlled teleportation to protect quantum messages. We expose forgeries, false allegation attacks and the possibility of repudiation by both parties.
  Fourthly, we focus on the AQS scheme by Zhang, Xin, Sun, Li and Li designed to sign classical messages without entangled states. We show that one can disavow the reception of messages, and that information-theoretic security is not achieved for other security goals.

AI.tldr: Security analysis paper exposing vulnerabilities in four recently proposed arbitrated quantum signature schemes, demonstrating repudiation attacks, forgeries, and false allegations across different quantum cryptographic approaches.
AI.motivation: To critically analyze the security claims of recently submitted arbitrated quantum signature (AQS) schemes by examining their vulnerabilities and demonstrating practical attacks that undermine their stated security goals.
AI.method: Systematic security analysis of four AQS schemes using cryptographic attack techniques: (1) Zhang et al.'s quantum message scheme with chained CNOT encryption, (2) Ding et al.'s classical message scheme based on GHZ states, (3) Lu et al.'s quantum message scheme using controlled teleportation, and (4) Zhang et al.'s classical message scheme without entangled states.
AI.result: Successfully demonstrated security vulnerabilities in all four schemes: sender repudiation, receiver repudiation, signature forgeries, false allegation attacks, and failure to achieve information-theoretic security. Each scheme was shown to be vulnerable to attacks that undermine their core security guarantees.
AI.conclusion: The analyzed AQS schemes fail to achieve their claimed security properties, highlighting the need for rigorous security proofs in quantum cryptographic protocol design and demonstrating that quantum communication alone does not guarantee security without proper protocol design.

title: Layered Quantum Architecture Search for 3D Point Cloud Classification
summary: We introduce layered Quantum Architecture Search (layered-QAS), a strategy inspired by classical network morphism that designs Parametrised Quantum Circuit (PQC) architectures by progressively growing and adapting them. PQCs offer strong expressiveness with relatively few parameters, yet they lack standard architectural layers (e.g., convolution, attention) that encode inductive biases for a given learning task. To assess the effectiveness of our method, we focus on 3D point cloud classification as a challenging yet highly structured problem. Whereas prior work on this task has used PQCs only as feature extractors for classical classifiers, our approach uses the PQC as the main building block of the classification model. Simulations show that our layered-QAS mitigates barren plateau, outperforms quantum-adapted local and evolutionary QAS baselines, and achieves state-of-the-art results among PQC-based methods on the ModelNet dataset.

AI.tldr: Layered-QAS is a quantum architecture search method that grows and adapts parametrized quantum circuits for 3D point cloud classification, achieving state-of-the-art PQC results while mitigating barren plateaus.
AI.motivation: Parametrized Quantum Circuits (PQCs) offer strong expressiveness with few parameters but lack standard architectural layers that encode inductive biases for specific learning tasks. Current approaches use PQCs only as feature extractors for classical classifiers rather than as the main building block of classification models.
AI.method: Layered Quantum Architecture Search (layered-QAS), inspired by classical network morphism, progressively grows and adapts PQC architectures. The approach designs PQC architectures specifically for 3D point cloud classification, using the PQC as the primary building block rather than just a feature extractor.
AI.result: Simulations show layered-QAS mitigates barren plateau problems, outperforms quantum-adapted local and evolutionary QAS baselines, and achieves state-of-the-art results among PQC-based methods on the ModelNet dataset for 3D point cloud classification.
AI.conclusion: Layered-QAS successfully addresses the lack of inductive biases in PQCs by providing an architecture search method that can design task-specific quantum circuits, demonstrating superior performance on structured problems like 3D point cloud classification while overcoming common quantum optimization challenges.

title: Variance reduction methods in the estimation of Pauli sums
summary: Accurately estimating expectation values of quantum observables with as few measurements as possible is crucial to many quantum computing applications. We introduce a framework that covers many of existing measurement strategies and introduce heuristics that can be used to enhance randomized schemes, including those based on Pauli grouping with inverse probability weighting and variants of the classical shadow algorithm. We show how to maximize information gain from such schemes, while carefully optimizing the distribution of possible measurements, and show that simple grouping algorithms can get close to, and in some cases exceed, state-of-the-art accuracy for unbiased estimation of expectation values on a standard quantum chemistry benchmark. We show how these randomized methods may be compared to more recent measurement schemes, such as shadow grouping, derandomized shadow, and overlapped grouping measurement, we show how the same strategies can be used to augment these schemes, and we demonstrate that we can reduce measurement costs by up to a factor of two by allowing Clifford measurement circuits for otherwise Clifford-less methods.

AI.tldr: A framework for optimizing quantum measurement strategies to minimize measurements while accurately estimating expectation values, showing grouping algorithms can match or exceed state-of-the-art accuracy and reduce costs by up to 2x.
AI.motivation: Accurately estimating expectation values of quantum observables with minimal measurements is crucial for quantum computing applications, requiring efficient measurement strategies to reduce resource requirements.
AI.method: Introduces a framework covering existing measurement strategies with heuristics to enhance randomized schemes (Pauli grouping with inverse probability weighting, classical shadow variants), optimizes measurement distribution to maximize information gain, and allows Clifford measurement circuits for otherwise Clifford-less methods.
AI.result: Simple grouping algorithms achieve close to or exceed state-of-the-art accuracy for unbiased expectation value estimation on quantum chemistry benchmarks; measurement costs reduced by up to factor of two using Clifford circuits.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables efficient comparison and enhancement of measurement schemes, demonstrating practical improvements in measurement efficiency for quantum computing applications through optimized grouping strategies and circuit adaptations.

title: Full Network Nonlocality Based Security In Quantum Key Distribution
summary: In the last decade research of quantum nonlocality has moved beyond the regime of standard Bell nonlocality to consider network-based experimental set-ups involving multiple independent sources. Notion of full network nonlocality has emerged as some truly network phenomena that cannot be realized in traditional Bell experiments. Present work manifests utility of such form of truly network non-classicality in designing a four partite network-based entanglement assisted quantum key distribution protocol. To be more precise, security of the protocol relies upon full network nonlocality detection via violation of some suitable trilocal inequality. Based on the quantum bit error rate and violation of trilocal inequality, arbitrary two qubit entangled states are characterized in accordance with their utility in successfully executing the protocol. Intuitively, owing to connected structure of entangled sources, any genuine form of network nonlocality may offer advantage over standard Bell nonlocality for designing secure key distribution protocols. To establish that as a fact, another QKD protocol relying upon Bell-CHSH nonlocality detection in all pairs of sender and a receiver party is designed. The former turns out to be more secure compared to the latter. Importantly, while the quantum bit error rate can be less than 14.6% exploiting Bell-CHSH nonlocality, it can be reduced below 13.7% by exploiting full network nonlocality.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes two quantum key distribution protocols: one using full network nonlocality in a four-partite network, and another using standard Bell-CHSH nonlocality. The network-based protocol proves more secure, achieving lower quantum bit error rates.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate the utility of full network nonlocality (a truly network phenomenon beyond standard Bell nonlocality) for designing more secure quantum key distribution protocols, showing advantages over traditional Bell-based approaches.
AI.method: Design two QKD protocols: 1) A four-partite network-based protocol using full network nonlocality detection via violation of trilocal inequalities, and 2) A protocol relying on Bell-CHSH nonlocality detection in all sender-receiver pairs. Compare security by analyzing quantum bit error rates and characterizing arbitrary two-qubit entangled states based on their utility in protocol execution.
AI.result: The network-based protocol using full network nonlocality is more secure than the Bell-CHSH based protocol. Quantum bit error rate can be reduced below 13.7% using full network nonlocality, compared to less than 14.6% using Bell-CHSH nonlocality.
AI.conclusion: Full network nonlocality offers security advantages over standard Bell nonlocality for quantum key distribution protocols, demonstrating that genuine network nonclassicality provides practical benefits in secure communication design.

title: Search-Driven Clause Learning for Product-State Quantum $k$-SAT (PRODSAT-QSAT)
summary: We study PRODSAT-QSAT($k$): given rank-one $k$-local projectors, determine whether a quantum $k$-SAT instance admits a satisfying product state. We present a CDCL-style refutation framework that searches a finite partition of each qubit's Bloch sphere while a sound theory solver checks region feasibility using a geometric overapproximation of the projection amplitudes for each constraint. When the theory solver proves that no state in a region can satisfy a constraint, it produces a sound conflict clause that blocks that region; accumulated blocking clauses can yield a global result of product-state unsatisfiability (UN-PRODSAT). We formalise the problem, prove the soundness of the clause-learning rule, and describe a practical algorithm and implementation.

AI.tldr: A CDCL-style refutation framework for determining product-state unsatisfiability in quantum k-SAT problems using geometric overapproximation and conflict clause learning.
AI.motivation: To develop a practical algorithmic approach for solving PRODSAT-QSAT(k) - determining whether quantum k-SAT instances admit satisfying product states, which is important for understanding quantum constraint satisfaction problems and their computational complexity.
AI.method: A CDCL-style refutation framework that searches a finite partition of each qubit's Bloch sphere while using a sound theory solver to check region feasibility via geometric overapproximation of projection amplitudes. The system produces conflict clauses when regions cannot satisfy constraints, accumulating blocking clauses to prove unsatisfiability.
AI.result: The paper formalizes the PRODSAT-QSAT(k) problem, proves soundness of the clause-learning rule, and describes a practical algorithm and implementation for determining product-state unsatisfiability.
AI.conclusion: The CDCL-style framework provides a sound and practical approach for proving product-state unsatisfiability in quantum k-SAT problems through geometric reasoning and conflict-driven clause learning.

title: Antenna Array Beamforming Based on a Hybrid Quantum Optimization Framework
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum optimization framework for large-scale antenna-array beamforming with jointly optimized discrete phases and continuous amplitudes. The method combines quantum-inspired search with classical gradient refinement to handle mixed discrete-continuous variables efficiently. For phase optimization, a Gray-code and odd-combination encoding scheme is introduced to improve robustness and avoid the complexity explosion of higher-order Ising models. For amplitude optimization, a geometric spin-combination encoding and a two-stage strategy are developed, using quantum-inspired optimization for coarse search and gradient optimization for fine refinement. To enhance solution diversity and quality, a rainbow quantum-inspired algorithm integrates multiple optimizers for parallel exploration, followed by hierarchical-clustering-based candidate refinement. In addition, a double outer-product method and an augmented version are proposed to construct the coupling matrix and bias vector efficiently, improving numerical precision and implementation efficiency. Under the scoring rules of the 7th National Quantum Computing Hackathon, simulations on a 32-element antenna array show that the proposed method achieves a score of 461.58 under constraints on near-main-lobe sidelobes, wide-angle sidelobes, beamwidth, and optimization time, nearly doubling the baseline score. The proposed framework provides an effective reference for beamforming optimization in future wireless communication systems.

AI.tldr: Hybrid quantum-classical framework for antenna beamforming with mixed discrete-continuous variables achieves near-doubled performance over baseline on 32-element array.
AI.motivation: Optimize large-scale antenna-array beamforming with jointly optimized discrete phases and continuous amplitudes, addressing the challenge of mixed discrete-continuous variables in quantum optimization frameworks.
AI.method: Combines quantum-inspired search with classical gradient refinement. Uses Gray-code/odd-combination encoding for phases, geometric spin-combination encoding for amplitudes with two-stage strategy (coarse quantum search + fine gradient refinement). Rainbow quantum-inspired algorithm integrates multiple optimizers for parallel exploration with hierarchical-clustering refinement. Double outer-product method constructs coupling matrix efficiently.
AI.result: Achieves score of 461.58 on 32-element antenna array under constraints (near-main-lobe sidelobes, wide-angle sidelobes, beamwidth, optimization time), nearly doubling the baseline score in 7th National Quantum Computing Hackathon.
AI.conclusion: Proposed hybrid quantum-classical framework provides effective reference for beamforming optimization in future wireless communication systems, demonstrating practical quantum-inspired optimization for mixed-variable problems.

title: Bright oxygen- and vacancy-derived spin-singlet diamond color centers with metastable spin triplets: OV$^{2+}$ and VOV$^{2+}$
summary: The ST1 diamond color center was experimentally demonstrated to involve a substitutional oxygen atom (O$_C$) and carbon vacancy (V$_C$), has a spin singlet ground-state, and a metastable electron spin ancilla: a triplet. ST1's structure was left unsolved for more than a decade. With embedded multiconfigurational quantum mechanical theory, we investigate O$_C$-V$_C$-derived diamond defects, specifically both 0 and +2-charged coupled O$_C$V$_C$, and O$_C$ surrounded by V$_C$s along the [110] axis (V$_C$O$_C$V$_C$). We found both O$_C$V$_{C}^{2+}$ (C$_{3v}$) and V$_C$O$_C$V$_{C}^{2+}$ (C$_{2v}$) to have a spin-singlet ground state (1$^1$A$_1$) and metastable spin triplets. We demonstrate ST1 to be V$_C$O$_C$V$_{C}^{2+}$. The calculated vertical excitation energies of V$_C$O$_C$V$_{C}^{2+}$'s first (1$^1$B$_2$) and second (2$^1$A$_1$) bright spin-singlet excited states closely match ST1's experimental zero phonon line (2.2-2.3 eV). O$_C$V$_{C}^{2+}$ ($^1$E) absorbs much higher (2.8 eV). The two O lone pairs favor V$_C$O$_C$V$_C$ over O$_C$V$_C$, in a similar manner as the single N lone pair favors formation of N$_C$V$_C$ centers.

AI.tldr: The ST1 diamond color center is identified as V_CO_CV_C^{2+} (C_{2v} symmetry), resolving a decade-long mystery about its atomic structure involving substitutional oxygen and carbon vacancies.
AI.motivation: The ST1 diamond color center's atomic structure remained unsolved for over a decade despite experimental evidence showing it involves a substitutional oxygen atom and carbon vacancy, with a spin singlet ground state and metastable triplet state.
AI.method: Used embedded multiconfigurational quantum mechanical theory to investigate O_C-V_C-derived diamond defects, specifically 0 and +2-charged coupled O_CV_C, and O_C surrounded by V_Cs along the [110] axis (V_CO_CV_C).
AI.result: Identified V_CO_CV_C^{2+} (C_{2v} symmetry) as the ST1 center, with calculated vertical excitation energies (2.2-2.3 eV for first and second bright spin-singlet excited states) matching experimental zero phonon line. O_CV_C^{2+} (C_{3v}) absorbs at much higher energy (2.8 eV).
AI.conclusion: The ST1 diamond color center is definitively identified as V_CO_CV_C^{2+}, with two oxygen lone pairs favoring this configuration over O_CV_C, analogous to how nitrogen lone pairs favor N_CV_C centers.

title: A single programmable photonic circuit for universal quantum measurements
summary: Programmable photonic quantum processors face a critical challenge: despite significant advances in quantum state preparation and manipulation, measurements remain limited to projective techniques. Here, we demonstrate a programmable measurement processor that overcomes this limitation by enabling arbitrary quantum measurements within a scalable circuit framework. Our large-scale integrated photonic architecture achieves precise coherent control of ancillary quantum systems, realizing a universal four-dimensional quantum measurement device. We benchmark the processor by performing measurement tomography on 100 randomly selected measurements, achieving an average fidelity of 97.7%. The processor's performance exceeds the theoretical limits of projective measurements in three key quantum information tasks: state discrimination (with 23 times lower error), state estimation (with 10.6% higher fidelity), and randomness generation (with 37% more randomness yield), demonstrating its high operational quality. This work establishes a fully programmable quantum measurement processor, advancing the development of universal quantum operations for photonic quantum information processing by providing the key missing component.

AI.tldr: Programmable photonic quantum processor enables arbitrary quantum measurements beyond projective limitations, achieving high-fidelity measurement tomography and superior performance in quantum information tasks.
AI.motivation: Current programmable photonic quantum processors are limited to projective measurements despite advances in state preparation and manipulation, creating a critical gap in achieving universal quantum operations.
AI.method: Developed a large-scale integrated photonic architecture with precise coherent control of ancillary quantum systems, creating a universal four-dimensional quantum measurement device within a scalable circuit framework.
AI.result: Achieved 97.7% average fidelity in measurement tomography on 100 randomly selected measurements. The processor outperforms projective measurement limits in state discrimination (23× lower error), state estimation (10.6% higher fidelity), and randomness generation (37% more yield).
AI.conclusion: This work establishes the first fully programmable quantum measurement processor, providing the key missing component for universal quantum operations in photonic quantum information processing.

title: Symmetric Resourceful Steady States via Non-Markovian Dissipation
comment: 5 pages and 4 figures (main); 6 pages and 1 figure (supplemental)
summary: We prove a no-go theorem for symmetry-based dissipative engineering of collective-spin steady states: in spin-only Lindblad dynamics with jump operators linear in the collective-spin operators, any unique steady state exhibiting at least $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry is necessarily the maximally mixed state. We then show that bath memory lifts this obstruction, enabling unique entangled steady states with a prescribed symmetry and a metrological gain, and providing a steady-state witness of non-Markovianity. Notably, this framework is largely insensitive to the microscopic details of the bath.

AI.tldr: No-go theorem: collective-spin steady states with Z2×Z2 symmetry in spin-only Markovian dynamics must be maximally mixed; bath memory enables unique entangled steady states with metrological gain.
AI.motivation: To understand limitations of symmetry-based dissipative engineering for collective-spin systems and explore how non-Markovian bath memory can overcome these limitations to create useful entangled steady states.
AI.method: Prove a no-go theorem for spin-only Lindblad dynamics with linear jump operators, then demonstrate how bath memory lifts this obstruction using theoretical analysis of non-Markovian dynamics.
AI.result: Any unique steady state with Z2×Z2 symmetry in Markovian collective-spin dynamics is necessarily maximally mixed; bath memory enables unique entangled steady states with prescribed symmetry and metrological gain, providing a steady-state witness of non-Markovianity.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry-based dissipative engineering of collective-spin steady states is fundamentally limited in Markovian settings but becomes possible with bath memory, offering a robust framework for generating entangled steady states largely insensitive to microscopic bath details.

title: Heisenberg-scaling characterization of an arbitrary two-channel network via two-port homodyne detection
summary: We present a fully Gaussian and experimentally feasible scheme for the simultaneous estimation of the four real parameters that characterize an arbitrary two-channel unitary transformation. The scheme utilizes a two-mode squeezed probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports, for which we derive the complete classical Fisher-information matrix analytically. Our scheme achieves the Heisenberg-scaling sensitivity for all four parameters simultaneously, enabling full multiparameter characterization of the generic two-channel interferometric device. We further show, by maximum-likelihood estimation, that the corresponding multiparameter Cramér-Rao bounds are saturated with a modest number of experimental repetitions and for low photon numbers. The scheme establishes a practical route to Heisenberg-scaling multiparameter Gaussian metrology for arbitrary two-channel networks, with direct relevance to calibration and sensing in integrated photonics and distributed quantum-enhanced measurement architectures.

AI.tldr: Gaussian scheme achieves Heisenberg-scaling multiparameter estimation for arbitrary two-channel unitaries using two-mode squeezed probes and balanced homodyne detection.
AI.motivation: To develop a practical, experimentally feasible method for full characterization of arbitrary two-channel unitary transformations with quantum-enhanced precision, addressing the need for calibration and sensing in integrated photonics and distributed quantum measurement architectures.
AI.method: Uses two-mode squeezed probe states and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports; derives complete classical Fisher-information matrix analytically; employs maximum-likelihood estimation to saturate Cramér-Rao bounds.
AI.result: Achieves Heisenberg-scaling sensitivity for all four parameters simultaneously; demonstrates saturation of multiparameter Cramér-Rao bounds with modest experimental repetitions and low photon numbers.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a practical route to Heisenberg-scaling multiparameter Gaussian metrology for arbitrary two-channel networks, enabling full characterization of generic two-channel interferometric devices.

title: Quantum inference on a classically trained quantum extreme learning machine
summary: Quantum extreme learning machines (QELMs) are unconventional computing architectures that bear remarkable promise in both classical and quantum machine-learning tasks, such as the estimate of quantum state properties. However, the probabilistic nature of quantum measurements demands extensive repetitions for training to precisely estimate expectation values, imposing stringent trade-offs among experimental resources, acquisition time, and signal-to-noise ratio, particularly for large datasets. Here we introduce a paradigm shift by harnessing the correspondence between stimulated and spontaneous emission. The QELM is trained exclusively with intense classical fields, yet it performs inference directly on previously unseen quantum input states to predict their quantum properties. This strategy dramatically reduces acquisition times while substantially enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio. Using frequency-bin-encoded biphoton states, implemented here for the first time in a quantum machine-learning architecture, we demonstrate entanglement witnessing of two-qubit states with (93 +- 4)% accuracy, multi-dimensional entanglement detection, and learning of the Hamiltonian governing photon-pair generation with a fidelity of (96 +- 4)%. By establishing classical training as a scalable route to quantum feature extraction, our results bridge macroscopic observables and nonclassical correlations, opening a new pathway toward faster and more robust quantum neural networks

AI.tldr: QELMs trained with classical fields perform quantum inference, reducing acquisition time and improving SNR for quantum property prediction tasks.
AI.motivation: Traditional QELMs require extensive quantum measurements for training, creating trade-offs between experimental resources, acquisition time, and signal-to-noise ratio, especially for large datasets.
AI.method: Harnessing stimulated-spontaneous emission correspondence to train QELMs exclusively with intense classical fields, then performing inference directly on quantum input states; implemented with frequency-bin-encoded biphoton states in a quantum machine-learning architecture.
AI.result: Demonstrated entanglement witnessing of two-qubit states with (93 ± 4)% accuracy, multi-dimensional entanglement detection, and learning of Hamiltonian governing photon-pair generation with (96 ± 4)% fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Classical training provides a scalable route to quantum feature extraction, bridging macroscopic observables and nonclassical correlations, and opening pathways toward faster, more robust quantum neural networks.

title: Certified Quantum Schrödinger Control via Hierarchical Tucker Models
summary: High-dimensional Schrödinger systems arising from tensor-product discretizations suffer from exponential state growth, making direct controller synthesis and real-time closed-loop simulation computationally challenging. Hierarchical Tucker (HT) tensor representations offer scalable low-rank surrogates, but the impact of fixed-rank truncation on closed-loop stability is not well understood. This paper develops a local robustness framework for sampled-data feedback control implemented with fixed-rank HT projections. By viewing each truncation as a bounded, rank-dependent perturbation of the nominal closed loop, and assuming a local phase-invariant contraction certificate together with trajectory-level hierarchical spectral decay, we show that the HT-projected dynamics are practically exponentially stable: trajectories converge to a dimension-independent tube whose radius decreases with the prescribed rank. We further obtain an explicit logarithmic rank-accuracy relation and establish conditions under which controllers designed on the HT-truncated surrogate model retain practical exponential tracking guarantees when deployed on the full system, together with an explicit bound quantifying the resulting surrogate-to-plant mismatch. A compact lattice example demonstrates the applicability of the framework.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a robustness framework for sampled-data feedback control using fixed-rank Hierarchical Tucker tensor representations, showing that HT-projected dynamics achieve practical exponential stability with dimension-independent error bounds.
AI.motivation: High-dimensional Schrödinger systems from tensor-product discretizations suffer from exponential state growth, making controller synthesis and real-time simulation computationally challenging. While HT tensor representations offer scalable low-rank surrogates, the impact of fixed-rank truncation on closed-loop stability is not well understood.
AI.method: Develops a local robustness framework viewing each truncation as a bounded, rank-dependent perturbation of the nominal closed loop. Assumes local phase-invariant contraction certificate together with trajectory-level hierarchical spectral decay to analyze stability of HT-projected dynamics.
AI.result: Shows HT-projected dynamics are practically exponentially stable: trajectories converge to a dimension-independent tube whose radius decreases with prescribed rank. Obtains explicit logarithmic rank-accuracy relation and establishes conditions under which controllers designed on HT-truncated surrogate models retain practical exponential tracking guarantees when deployed on full systems.
AI.conclusion: Provides theoretical framework for stability guarantees in fixed-rank HT tensor control of high-dimensional systems, with explicit bounds on surrogate-to-plant mismatch and demonstration of applicability through a compact lattice example.
